title: Frame grammar vector record
description: One language-neutral conformance fixture for the frame grammar and content_version minting defined by docs/frame-grammar-v1.md: either a frame's role_keys/rows against its canonical bytes and minted content_version, a content_version preimage's inputs against its minted token, or a collection's members against its minted token -- or, for a negative vector, the same kind of input against the stable category it is refused under. See the README beside this schema for field semantics, the positive/negative split, the three record kinds, and the frozen failure_category vocabulary.

format_version.description: The vector record format's own version. Pinned to the version this schema validates; a vector claiming a different format_version must validate against that version's own schema instead. Distinct from FRAME_GRAMMAR_VERSION (the published grammar document's own semver) and from frame_version/identity_version (the byte-rule domain separators hashed into canonical bytes).

name.description: The vector's stable, unique, kebab-case id. Matches the stem of the file it lives in, so a file rename is a rename of the vector.

description.description: One-line, human-readable statement of what the vector proves.

kind.description: Which of the three record shapes this vector carries. "frame": role_keys/rows exercised through Frame.build and canonical_frame_bytes, then through content_version minting. "content_version": a content_version preimage's inputs (frame_sha256 plus the same content_version_input shape) exercised through content_version minting alone, independent of any frame -- used for preimage-level refusals that a full frame build would never reach. "collection_content_version": a collection's members exercised through collection-level minting.

classification.description: positive: the input builds (and, where applicable, mints a token) without refusal. negative: the input is refused, and no expected output exists to check.

coverage.description: Non-normative dot-separated tags naming what this vector exercises (e.g. "columns.reserved-collision", "rows.duplicate-key"). Free to grow; not a frozen vocabulary like failure_category.

notes.description: Optional free-form context: why the vector is shaped this way, a pointer to the grammar rule it enforces, or a caveat for a reader of the fixture.

role_keys.description: kind: "frame" only. The shape's declared entity role property references, in whatever order they were declared -- column order is a derived property, not an input.

rows.description: kind: "frame" only. The frame's input rows: a JSON array of objects, each keyed by column name. This is the frame's pre-canonicalisation input, in whatever order the vector author chose to type it in; input row order carries no meaning.

expected_columns.description: kind: "frame", positive only. The exact columns array a conformant implementation must derive from role_keys.

canonical_bytes.description: kind: "frame", positive only. The exact JCS bytes of expected_document, lossless hex-encoded.

expected_document.description: kind: "frame", positive only. The fully normalised closed frame document ({frame_version, columns, rows}) canonical_bytes must be the JCS serialisation of -- present so a reader, or the standalone validator, can check canonical_bytes independently of any particular implementation's row-construction logic. Compared by structural JSON equality; key order here is not meaningful. Byte-for-byte comparison only enters at canonical_bytes itself.

expected_frame_sha256.description: kind: "frame", positive only. The full 64 lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the bytes decoded from canonical_bytes -- also the frame_sha256 member a conformant content_version preimage must carry.

content_version_input.description: kind: "frame" (positive only) or "content_version" (either classification). The content_version preimage inputs beyond frame_sha256: graph_revision, source_revisions, facets, and optionally conversion (the record object or a manifest trace's one-entry conversion array) -- exactly the named-argument shape content_version minting accepts. Left loosely typed here (not further constrained by this schema) because a negative content_version vector's whole point is to carry a shape this schema's own domain rules would otherwise have to duplicate and could get out of step with.

frame_sha256.description: kind: "content_version" only. The frame_sha256 supplied directly as a content_version minting input, since this kind exercises preimage-level rules independent of any actual frame.

expected_preimage.description: kind: "frame" or "content_version" (positive only): the closed content_version preimage document minting must build from frame_sha256 plus content_version_input. kind: "collection_content_version" (positive only): the closed collection preimage document ({identity_version, members}) built from members, sorted by spec_id. Present so canonical_bytes-equivalent independence holds one level up: expected_content_version must be exactly "cv_" plus the first 32 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256(JCS(expected_preimage)).

expected_content_version.description: Positive only, any kind. The full public cv_-prefixed token minting must produce.

members.description: kind: "collection_content_version" only. An array of two-element [spec_id, content_version] arrays, each carrying a full public token string, in whatever order the vector author chose to type them in. Left loosely typed (plain strings, no token-shape pattern) so a negative vector can carry a deliberately malformed token.

failure_category.description: Negative only. The stable failure category the input is refused under. See the README beside this schema for the frozen vocabulary, each category's definition, and which module raises it.
